deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 75-77): Grothendieck takes an arrangement Sigma of pseudo-lines in a real projective plane X. He wants to build a 'dual' surface \mathcal{X} together with a cell complex K. The vertices of K are the 'stable' pseudo-lines D, meaning pseudo-lines in general position with respect to Sigma, taken up to isotopy. The edges are 'transition arcs': specialisation arcs, where D sweeps across a vertex of Sigma by a triangle flip ('basculement'), and their antipodes. The 2-cells are polygons. Page 75 begins a combinatorial description of K as a graph Gamma: vertices are the stable p.d. D, oriented edges are pairs (D,a) with a a transition arc for D. This page completes the description. It amounts to a 'map' or ribbon-graph presentation of a possibly non-orientable surface:
(1) An involution on oriented edges ('opposite'). The opposite of (D,a) is (D',a'). Here D' is obtained from D by flipping it toward the antipodal endpoint antip(a), and a' is obtained from a by parallel transport ('opposite to a'). The origin of (D,a) is D.
(2) A polygonal (cyclic) structure on the set of oriented edges issuing from D, described as 'obvious'. This is a rotation system.
(3) Orientation-transport data along edges, given as the inverse of the parallel transport of orientations. In modern terms this is a signed rotation system / general embedding scheme.
He then tests the construction against the expected local structure at 'super-singular' points. The next page shows these are the points delta_i of the dual plane X^vee that correspond to the lines D_i of Sigma when Sigma consists of straight lines. In that case \mathcal{X} should reproduce X^vee, or its double cover, with the dual line arrangement.
Result of the test:
- With recipe (3) as stated, the circuits around super-singular points come out wrong.
- If (3) is replaced by plain parallel transport, the circuits come out right, but then there is no natural map \mathcal{X} -> X.
He proposes a second gluing: glue a to b' and b to a' (sheets at a flip), using parallel transport. The coloured sketch shows the two lines omega_D, omega_D', hatched families of sheets, and orientations omega_F, omega_F' of faces. The red cross most likely marks the crossing at the flipped vertex. This gluing yields a map \mathcal{X} -> X. It is no longer an immersion: it folds/branches along the edges of K. The combinatorics are the same except in (1), where the opposite of (D,a) is now (D',a') with a' the parallel transport of a. The next page concludes that this recipe is again unsatisfactory for the super-singular circuits unless (3) is reversed. Overall purpose: a combinatorial-topological construction of the 'space of pseudo-lines' (the dual) of a pseudo-line arrangement as a cell-decomposed surface with antipodal involution, checked against projective duality in the stretchable case.
errors: No outright mathematical error. The page is exploratory and Grothendieck himself records that each recipe fails one requirement: correct circuits around super-singular points, or existence of a natural map to X. The claim that the polygonal structure (2) is 'évidente' is unproved. The compatibility conditions needed for (1)-(3) to define a closed surface are not checked on this page.

ideas.what: Description of the dual surface via a graph with an involution on oriented edges, a cyclic order at vertices and orientation-transport data
ideas.modern_name: signed rotation system / general embedding scheme (combinatorial map for non-orientable surfaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heffter, Edmonds (orientable); Ringel, Youngs, Stahl, Mohar-Thomassen (signed/general embedding schemes)
ideas.where_published: Combinatorial maps / dessins appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this signed version for pseudo-line duals

ideas.what: Space of stable pseudo-lines of an arrangement, with flips across vertices as edges, organised into a surface with antipodal involution
ideas.modern_name: cellular model of the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (single-element extensions / pseudo-line extensions; dual arrangement via Goodman-Pollack duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, flips/mutations); Goodman-Pollack (1980s); Sturmfels-Ziegler (1993, extension spaces); Goodman-Pollack-Wenger-Zamfirescu (1994)

ideas.what: Test of the construction against projective duality: for straight lines \mathcal{X} should be the dual plane, with special 'super-singular' points delta_i
Alternative gluing producing a map \mathcal{X} -> X that folds along the edges of K rather than being an immersion
ideas.modern_name: folded / branched map from the dual surface to the plane

missed.claim: Grothendieck's surface \mathcal{X} of stable pseudo-lines, with flip edges and antipodal involution, is essentially a cell model of the space of single-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid. Its homotopy type is the subject of the Sturmfels-Ziegler extension-space problem. He is in effect trying to show, cellularly, that this space is a surface (2-sphere/projective plane) recovering the dual plane. This anticipates later oriented-matroid work and is not credited to him.
missed.quote: Origine de (D,a) est D / 2) Structure polygonale sur l'un des arêtes orientées issues de D: évidente
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An explicit combinatorial-map description of the rank-3 extension space, if it can be completed, would give a direct proof that it is a surface. It would also show how super-singular points (the original lines) sit inside it.

missed.claim: Neither recipe simultaneously gives the correct local structure at super-singular points and a natural map \mathcal{X} -> X. The page leaves open how to choose the orientation-transport rule (3) so that both hold.
missed.quote: on trouve les bons circuits super-singuliers (mais pas d'application naturelle \mathcal{X}\to X!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise, small open design question about a canonical dual surface for non-stretchable arrangements. It could be settled with modern oriented-matroid tools.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a well-informed but exploratory construction of the dual 'space of pseudo-lines' of an arrangement as a signed ribbon-graph surface. It closely parallels later extension-space work in oriented matroid theory, which is a modestly interesting uncredited anticipation. Nothing on the page is finished, and the techniques themselves are standard.
transcription_corrections: 'Feuilletons on ne trouve pas' should read 'Hélas on ne trouve pas'.
'circuits superorthogonaux' should read 'circuits super-singuliers' (consistent with the next page).
'c'est des feuillets à b: b : a', ainsi' is probably 'c'est de recoller a à b', b à a', ainsi' (matching a_D: a -> b' on the previous page).
'mais application en plusieurs le long des arêtes' is probably 'mais application se (re)pliant le long des arêtes de K' (a folding map).
'paraison!' at the start of the line after 'l'instant' is a word fragment ('...paraison!'), not 'l'instant [?]'.
In 1), '{+rien+}' above the line is likely an insertion such as 'ici' or similar; uncertain.
